name: The Sierra Club Foundation: climate and clean energy (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a tonne of greenhouse gas kept out of the air spares people everywhere (heat deaths), so the result is spread by world population; the small US coal and traffic smoke share is left in the world figure.
summary: The Sierra Club Foundation is the 501(c)(3) that funds the Sierra Club's charitable campaigns; this model is its climate work in 2022-2024: its Beyond Coal grants ($17.1M in 2024) and, by our judgment, half its other grants to the Sierra Club ($52.3M in 2024 in all). It counts the US coal plants that closed in 2022-2024 (advocacy credited with 15%, the Sierra Club with 40% of that and the Foundation with 70% of the Sierra Club's resources) and the Sierra Club's shares of EPA's 2023 methane rule, its 2024 power-plant and vehicle standards and California's Advanced Clean Cars II, at the same tonnes, status and steps as the other climate models, plus 50% for gas pipelines, export terminals and other wins. At the defaults a dollar given averts about 0.016 tonnes of CO₂e (about $64 a tonne), {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, about four fifths of the tonnes from the coal closings; Beyond Coal is the field's largest campaign against the coal plants that closed, but most closings were utilities' economic choices and the federal rules have since been weakened or repealed. The biggest uncertainties are the years a won reform counts, the missing-data discount and advocacy's share of the closings; every branch is discounted for missing data, since no tonne is measured for the Sierra Club's work.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: For each win: what would have happened anyway, the Sierra Club's share of the advocacy and the Foundation's part of the Sierra Club's resources, and how much is delivered; then the evidence and missing-data steps, the other wins and the side effects.

sections.title: Air pollution these tonnes carry
sections.explainer: Every tonne avoids its heat deaths; a tonne from burning less coal or petrol near people also avoids air-pollution deaths. These rows say how much of the shared air-pollution rate applies to these tonnes, and how much of them is methane (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

sections.title: Other outcomes, in tonnes
sections.explainer: The public money won for US households (units of value) is counted in its own unit and enters the tonnes only through the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6).

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per year of the period, per dollar of a typical year's cost.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind; and the next dollar does less than the period's average.

source.quote: SECURING THE RETIREMENT OR COMMITTMENT TO RETIRE OUR 389TH COAL PLANT SINCE THE CAMPAIGN BEGAN IN 2010

rows.explainer: Beyond Coal is the field's largest campaign against coal plants (funded by Bloomberg Philanthropies through the Foundation; $76.7M of the Foundation's grants in 2022-2024), with organisers, lawyers and analysts in utility-commission cases, permit fights and local campaigns in most coal states; it counts 389 plants retired or committed to retire since 2010, of about 530. Others: Earthjustice, often its counsel (10% in its model), state and local groups, NRDC, the Environmental Defense Fund and the other Bloomberg grantees. Our judgment, 40% (20% to 60%) of the advocacy behind the period's closings, so that with Earthjustice's 10% the named groups take half, leaving the rest to the others; the Sierra Club claims a part in most closings, which names them, not its share (climate.md).

rows.label: EPA methane rule: the Sierra Club's share of the advocacy behind it
rows.explainer: The Sierra Club commented and mobilised supporters for EPA's methane rule and joined the groups defending it in court, but the Environmental Defense Fund led the field (25% in its model), beside Clean Air Task Force (10%), Earthjustice (8%), NRDC, Earthworks and state groups. Our judgment, 5% (2% to 12%), below Earthjustice's because oil and gas methane is not one of the Sierra Club's lead campaigns; the four modelled groups' shares sum to under half.

Others: the Environmental Defense Fund, Clean Air Task Force and Earthjustice (10% each in their models), the Union of Concerned Scientists (3%), NRDC and states. Our judgment, 10% (4% to 25%), the same as the other leading groups', so the modelled groups' shares sum to 43%.

source.title: Sierra Club, Form 990 for 2024 (IRS e-file XML, object 202503169349309600), Schedule O, Part III line 4a
source.quote: OUR BEYOND DIRTY FUELS CAMPAIGN PROTECTED COMMUNITIES, LANDSCAPES, AND WILDLIFE FROM 11 DANGEROUS GAS PIPELINES, 25 LIQUEFIED METHANE GAS EXPORT PROJECTS, AND FOUR OIL EXPORT FACILITIES.

rows.explainer: The five branches are the period's largest countable climate wins; the rest of the work isn't in them: Beyond Dirty Fuels' gas pipelines and export terminals blocked or delayed (11 pipelines, 25 gas export projects and four oil export facilities in 2024 alone, by its count) and its part in the federal pause on new gas-export approvals (2024), new gas plants opposed, EPA's heavy-duty truck standards and California's clean-fleet and locomotive rules, transport electrification in 14 states' utility dockets, the clean school bus and ports programmes, and the chapters' state and city clean-energy work. Their spending is in the cost, so leaving them out would count them as worth nothing. Our judgment, 50% (20% to 100%), as Earthjustice's for similar state and gas work and above Clean Air Task Force's 30% for a specialist's other wins.

rows.label: Side effect: slower nuclear power from the Sierra Club's opposition to it, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: The Sierra Club opposes nuclear power, including the extension of California's Diablo Canyon plant (2022); where opposition closes or delays a reactor, gas and coal fill part of the gap. -2% (-10% to 0), our judgment, as for the Union of Concerned Scientists' safety campaigns: Diablo Canyon's extension passed despite it, and no closure in the period is attributed to it.

rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.us_oil_gas_methane_rule_voc_deaths_per_year): EPA's 56 (2028) to 74 (2038) local ozone deaths a year from the rule's cut in volatile organic compounds, as in Earthjustice's model.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly (the methane rule's local smog)
rows.explainer: The methane rule's local ozone deaths per tonne of its methane, × the methane share, so per average tonne of this model: they share the tonnes' credit and wait steps. Fuel smoke is in the air-pollution weight; methane's own ozone and earlier warming are in the shared conversion through the methane share.

rows.formula: compliance_uov_per_year / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)
rows.explainer: Units of value into tonnes at what a tonne of these is worth on the site's scale (its heat and air-pollution deaths by age, as the conversion counts them), the bridge Environmental Defense Fund's model uses (docs/normalization.md 2.6).

rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_oil_gas_methane_rule_net_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2019 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * usmeth_downstream / usmeth_tonnes_per_year * usmeth_counterfactual_adj * usmeth_attribution_share * usmeth_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21): operators' net cost after the gas they recover and sell (EPA's regulatory impact analysis, $1.5 billion a year), in 2019 dollars moved to 2024's, valued as money lost by those who bear it, consumers and owners (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple, 1.2 times average US consumption), on the log scale; over the same years and wait as the rule's benefits, with the branch's chance, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step, not its evidence adjustment (which is about the benefits).
